status_summary: Executive Order 14154 (2025-01-20) directed agencies to pause disbursements under Inflation Reduction Act and infrastructure law programs, EPA terminated $20 billion in Greenhouse Gas Reduction Fund awards to eight entities on 2025-03-11 and said on 2025-08-07 it would stop implementing the $7 billion Solar for All program, and Public Law 119-21, section 60002 (2025-07-04), repealed Clean Air Act section 134, the fund's authorizing provision. On 2025-09-02 a D.C. Circuit panel ruled 2-1 for EPA, but on 2026-08-04 the en banc court reversed that decision and upheld the preliminary injunction against the March 2025 terminations (by six of ten judges, per the Columbia Sabin Center), and, as JURIST reports, stayed its judgment to let EPA ask the Supreme Court to intervene, so those funds remain frozen (the date and form of the stay are unverified). On Solar for All, the District of Rhode Island on 2026-09-18 declared the program's termination unlawful and vacated it, and the District of Columbia on 2026-09-22 vacated EPA's policy-level decision that the program could no longer operate (without reviewing individual grant terminations); both held that the 2025 law ended new grant authority and rescinded only unobligated balances, both declined injunctions beyond vacatur, and no appeal or stay was found in the sources read. The statutory repeal of new grant authority remains in effect while both sets of terminations of obligated funds are held unlawful or enjoined, and EPA's program page, updated 2026-09-09, does not mention the 2026 rulings.

timeline.event: Executive Order 14154 directs agencies to pause disbursement of funds under Inflation Reduction Act and Infrastructure Investment and Jobs Act programs pending review (published in the Federal Register 2025-01-29).

EPA terminates $20 billion in Greenhouse Gas Reduction Fund awards to eight entities (including Climate United Fund, Coalition for Green Capital and Power Forward Communities), citing conflicts of interest and oversight concerns; these are EPA's characterizations.

Public Law 119-21, title VI, section 60002 (139 Stat. 154), repeals Clean Air Act section 134 (42 U.S.C. 7434), the Greenhouse Gas Reduction Fund provision; EPA's page describes the law as also rescinding the fund's money, and later court rulings read the rescission as reaching only unobligated balances.
EPA announces it will stop implementing the $7 billion Solar for All program; EPA's page says the 2025 law repealed its authority and rescinded remaining funds.

The D.C. Circuit rules 2-1 for EPA, vacating a district court injunction that had blocked the terminations and holding that the grantees' claims are essentially contractual, so jurisdiction lies with the Court of Federal Claims (as described on EPA's page; the opinion itself was not fetched).

EPA's fiscal year 2027 Budget in Brief describes some pass-through funding as not directly protecting the environment and proposes $305 million for the clean water and drinking water state revolving funds (document filed under April 2026, exact day not confirmed, first of month used).

The D.C. Circuit, sitting en banc in Climate United Fund v. Citibank (Nos. 25-5122 and 25-5123), issues a per curiam judgment on the preliminary injunction against the Greenhouse Gas Reduction Fund terminations, which per the Columbia Sabin Center upholds the injunction by a six to four vote and reverses the 2025-09-02 panel; a same-day order dissolves the April 2025 administrative stay effective seven days later and directs issuance of the mandate.
timeline.source: D.C. Circuit (via Leagle and an order copy hosted by Inclusiv)

timeline.event: The D.C. Circuit stays its judgment to let EPA seek Supreme Court review, keeping the National Clean Investment Fund and Clean Communities Investment Accelerator funds frozen, as JURIST reports in its account of the 2026-08-04 ruling; the date and terms of the stay were not confirmed from a court document (the 2026-08-07 date comes from a grantee-side update and is an unverified lead at low confidence).

In Rhode Island AFL-CIO v. EPA (D.R.I., No. 1:25-cv-00510), Judge Mary McElroy grants the plaintiffs' motion for summary judgment and denies EPA's cross-motion, declares EPA's termination of the Solar for All program unlawful under the APA as contrary to law and in excess of statutory authority, and vacates it; the court reads the 2025 law as repealing new grant authority and rescinding only unobligated balances, declines a permanent injunction because vacatur suffices, and does not reach the arbitrary-and-capricious or constitutional claims. EPA said it was considering an appeal (per OPB).
timeline.source: U.S. District Court for the District of Rhode Island

timeline.event: In Harris County, Texas v. EPA (D.D.C., No. 1:25-cv-03646), Judge Tanya Chutkan holds EPA's policy-level Elimination Decision (that the 2025 law made continued operation of Solar for All impermissible) arbitrary and capricious, contrary to law and in excess of statutory authority, and vacates it, declining to limit vacatur to the county's own grant and not reviewing individual grant terminations; the court reads the 2025 law as rescinding only unobligated balances, grants the government summary judgment on the ultra vires and constitutional claims, denies an injunction without prejudice, and says a separate order will be entered.
timeline.source: U.S. District Court for the District of Columbia

uncertainties: The en banc judgment of 2026-08-04 was read only in part (its caption and opening disposition line on Leagle); its outcome and vote are taken from the Columbia Sabin Center and JURIST. A same-day D.C. Circuit order dissolving the administrative stay and directing the mandate was read from a copy hosted by a grantee-side organization; the date and terms of the stay of the judgment are not confirmed by a court document: JURIST, in its undated account of the 2026-08-04 ruling, reports that the court stayed its judgment to let EPA seek Supreme Court review (so it may describe the same-day order); an update by that grantee-side organization reports an extension of the administrative stay on 2026-08-07 (an unverified lead at low confidence); and the Civil Rights Litigation Clearinghouse case page reports a motion to stay the mandate dated 2026-08-08, granted 2026-08-09 and running through 2026-11-09, dates that fall on a weekend and conflict with the other account. Whether EPA has filed a Supreme Court petition was not found. The district court rulings of 2026-09-18 (D.R.I., ECF 48, on the courtlistener storage host) and 2026-09-22 (D.D.C., Doc. 58, on cases.justia.com) were read on court copies in this pass. The District of Columbia opinion says a separate order will be entered, and that order was not located; it vacates the policy-level Elimination Decision and does not review the county's individual grant termination, so earlier descriptions of it as a vacatur of the termination are narrowed. The Rhode Island order does not reach the arbitrary-and-capricious or constitutional claims. Appeal or stay status comes only from press and searches and was not verified on a docket. Section 60002 of Public Law 119-21 was confirmed through the 42 U.S.C. 7434 notes on law.cornell.edu; the rescission wording and other IRA grant rescissions in the law were not read. Most grant facts come from one EPA web page that presents EPA's characterizations of the grantees. Proceedings in the Court of Federal Claims were not checked. Searched 2026-10-26: no appeal, stay or certiorari filing on the Solar for All vacaturs (2026-09-18 and 2026-09-22) was found; a law firm page of 2026-10-08 only restates the 2026-09-22 ruling.
